Lesson 6 · Business route

Prediction that survives new cases

Which dispatch-cost forecast is useful for future jobs?

The business problem

A dispatch firm quotes jobs before the final service cost is known. Underquoting hurts margin; quoting too high may lose the customer. Dispatchers know some facts at intake, such as job size and route, but they learn others only after the work is done. The firm wants a forecast that uses information available when a quote must be issued and that improves the commercial decision, not merely a score on a historical file.

What the data show

On the final test jobs, the simple baseline has root-mean-square error 37.05 credits; the selected procedure has 23.56 credits.

The team compares a simple baseline with a selected forecasting procedure on jobs kept out of model choice. Root-mean-square error puts extra weight on large misses, which is useful when big surprises matter. It still does not distinguish an underquote from an overquote in terms of profit. The pricing team should therefore read the error score alongside the pattern of misses on costly jobs, the margin rule, and how often staff would need to override a suggested quote.

What would you decide?

Choose the loss that matches costly mistakes, learn every preparation step within development data, and open the final test only after freezing the procedure. Monitor performance when conditions change.

Try the procedure in a limited quoting workflow. Record its proposed quote, the dispatcher’s final quote, realized cost, customer acceptance, and the reason for each override. Route jobs with missing or unusual inputs to a review path. Decide in advance what would count as success: fewer damaging underquotes, acceptable win rates, and manageable staff effort. That turns a model comparison into a controlled operating decision.

Pause and explain

What should dispatchers track during a limited quoting trial?

Compare your reasoning

Track underquotes, realized margins, unusual jobs, customer acceptance, and staff overrides alongside average prediction error.

Check your judgment

Reveal the case’s known answer

The case makes job cost depend on information available at intake plus unpredictable variation. The selected procedure improves the test error; a limited trial shows whether that improvement helps quoting.
